1.question:
What is the name and description of the business topic you want to create?

Provide a short **topic name** (e.g. "Customer Churn & Retention") and a **1–3 sentence description** explaining what this topic is about, what business question it answers, and who the primary audience is.
1.answer: Customer Success Management. Covers: Customer Success Management, Customer Product Onboarding, Partner Ecosystem Performance, Feature Adoption Tracking, Customer Risk Intervention (CTA) (+5 more)

6.question:
What business rules and definitions should the AI know when answering questions in the **Customer Success Management** topic?

Pre-populated definitions are drawn from your selected concepts, datasets, and columns. **Confirm the ones that apply, edit wording where needed, and add custom rules** your team uses that aren't listed below — e.g. specific health score thresholds, territory exclusions, or fiscal quarter conventions.

selected.label: CTA = Gainsight Call-to-Action (leading risk signal, NOT confirmed churn)
selected.description: A CTA (Call-to-Action) is a triggered risk intervention record created in Gainsight when a customer account meets predefined risk thresholds. CTAs represent leading indicators that require CSM investigation — they do NOT confirm a customer will churn. CTA_ARR quantifies the ARR exposed to risk at the moment the CTA is opened, and should never be treated as lost ARR unless the CTA closes as churned.
selected.ai_reasoning: The term 'CTA' is central to the Customer Risk Intervention concept and appears across both GS_CTA_SUMMARY and GS_CTA_CAMPAIGN; without this definition the AI will conflate open CTAs with confirmed churn, inflating at-risk ARR figures.

selected.label: Churn ≠ Downgrade: CHURN_DATE populated = full cancellation; DOWNGRADE_AMOUNT > 0 without CHURN_DATE = partial contraction
selected.description: In the CHURN DATASET, an account is classified as churned only when CHURN_DATE is populated. An account with a non-zero DOWNGRADE_AMOUNT but no CHURN_DATE is a downgrade (partial ARR contraction), not a full cancellation. These are mutually exclusive states — do not aggregate them without explicit filtering. AP_SPREAD_PCT captures the percentage contraction for downgrades.
selected.ai_reasoning: Churn and downgrade records coexist in the same CHURN DATASET under the Customer Churn & Downgrade concept; conflating them overstates churn volume and understates the true downgrade population.

selected.label: High Risk Account = low Gainsight health score AND an active open CTA in GS_CTA_SUMMARY (note: app label reads 'Hisk Risk' — known typo)
selected.description: An account is 'High Risk' when its Gainsight health score falls below the defined threshold AND an active (open) CTA record exists in GS_CTA_SUMMARY. The formal metrics 'CMP - High Risk Accounts' and 'CMP - High Risk Accounts ARR' measure this population — note the label typo ('Hisk Risk') in the app is a known data entry error, not a separate category. Accounts with a low health score but no active CTA are 'at risk' but not classified as 'high risk'.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both CMP - High Risk Accounts metrics were selected in step 4 and the app contains a known label typo; this rule prevents the AI from treating 'Hisk Risk' as a distinct tier or missing the correct metric by name.

selected.label: ICP Account for CS purposes = ICP_ACCOUNT flag in DWH_RENEWAL_OPPORTUNITY or Product - Opportunities (not the firmographic ICP flag)
selected.description: For Customer Success renewal prioritisation, the authoritative ICP flag is ICP_ACCOUNT in either DWH_RENEWAL_OPPORTUNITY or Product - Opportunities. This flag drives which accounts receive dedicated CSM effort at renewal. The ICP_ACCOUNT column in firmographic/Account Universe datasets serves marketing targeting and uses a different definition — do not substitute one for the other when filtering renewal pipelines.
selected.ai_reasoning: ICP_ACCOUNT appears in multiple datasets selected across steps 3 and 5 with subtly different business meanings; without this rule the AI may pull the wrong ICP definition when scoping renewal queries.

selected.label: BRAVE = Budget / Risk / Alternatives / Value / Evaluation — use BRAVE_TYPE_GC (not REASON_NAME) to classify CTA intervention type
selected.description: BRAVE is Optimizely's internal CSM intervention taxonomy. Each CTA in GS_CTA_SUMMARY is categorised by BRAVE_TYPE_GC into one of the five BRAVE dimensions. When grouping or filtering CTAs by intervention type, always use BRAVE_TYPE_GC as the canonical field — REASON_NAME varies by territory and campaign and is not standardised for cross-regional comparison.
selected.ai_reasoning: BRAVE_TYPE_GC is a key segmentation column on the Customer Risk Intervention (CTA) concept and was selected in step 3; defining BRAVE prevents the AI from treating it as an unknown acronym and from using the non-standardised REASON_NAME as a substitute.

selected.label: Active user = ACTIVE_USERS_30D (30-day rolling window); do NOT use TOTAL_USERS_WITH_ACCESS as a proxy for active usage
selected.description: In the context of Customer Health Monitoring, an active user is any licensed user who performed a product action within the last 30 calendar days, as captured by ACTIVE_USERS_30D in Active_Users_Projects_Workspaces. This signal feeds the multi-signal health score that triggers CTA creation. TOTAL_USERS_WITH_ACCESS represents licensed seat count — an account with 500 licensed seats but 2 active users in 30 days is disengaged, not healthy.
selected.ai_reasoning: ACTIVE_USERS_30D is the primary engagement signal driving health scores and CTA triggers; without this rule the AI conflates licensed seats with actual product activity, producing misleading health assessments.

selected.label: Feature 'adopted' = in Feature Adoption Matrix Account; 'not yet adopted' = in Features Not Adopted Account — never combine without explicit filtering
selected.description: Feature adoption uses two complementary datasets. A feature is adopted by an account only if it appears in 'Feature Adoption Matrix Account' (positive confirmation). 'Features Not Adopted Account' lists features the account is licensed for but has not yet used — these are upsell and CSM intervention opportunities. Combining both datasets without a filter produces double-counting. TECHNOLOGY_MATURITY and IS_OPTI_ONE are valid segmentation dimensions on both datasets.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both datasets were selected in step 3 under Feature Adoption Tracking; the two-dataset structure is non-obvious and the AI must know they represent opposite adoption states to avoid double-counting.

7.question: Several terms used in the **Customer Success Management** topic also appear in other Optimizely Analytics topics with different meanings. Confirm the intended interpretation for each ambiguous term below — pre-selected rows reflect the meaning that aligns with your step 2–6 choices. Deselect any already sufficiently clear, and use **Add custom disambiguation** for any additional terms your team finds confusing.

selected.label: "Onboarding" = CSM-managed Customer Product Onboarding (GS_ONBOARDING_CUSTOMERS) — NOT Opal's in-app onboarding wizard
selected.description: Two structurally distinct onboarding flows exist in the graph. In this topic, 'onboarding' refers exclusively to the Gainsight-managed, CSM-owned structured engagement delivered post-sale across product lines, tracked in GS_ONBOARDING_CUSTOMERS (ENGAGEMENT_NAME, ELEMENT_NAME, STAGE, PRODUCT_GROUP). It does NOT refer to Opal Onboarding — the automated in-app product wizard guiding new Opal AI users, tracked in Product - Opal Onboarding Snapshots and Userflow Data. Any query about onboarding completion, stage progression, or product group onboarding coverage must resolve to GS_ONBOARDING_CUSTOMERS only.
selected.ai_reasoning: The graph contains an explicit `distinct-from` edge between Customer Product Onboarding (selected in step 2) and Opal Onboarding (not selected), and both concepts share the word 'onboarding' in dataset names across the app — creating a high collision risk whenever a CSM asks an unqualified onboarding question.

selected.label: DWH_CS_EXPERIMENTATION_USAGE in this topic = CSM product-stickiness health signal, NOT an A/B experimentation analytics source
selected.description: DWH_CS_EXPERIMENTATION_USAGE is referenced by both the Customer Success Management concept (selected) and the A/B Experimentation / Feature Experimentation (FX) concepts (not selected in this topic). Within this CSM topic, this dataset is used exclusively to measure whether a customer account is creating and running experiments — a product engagement and stickiness indicator for health assessment. It should NOT be used to analyse experiment outcomes, statistical results, variant performance, or test methodology — those queries belong to the A/B Experimentation topic and should be routed there.
selected.ai_reasoning: DWH_CS_EXPERIMENTATION_USAGE has `composes` edges into both the Customer Success Management and the A/B Experimentation / Feature Experimentation (FX) Usage & Entitlement concept clusters; without this rule the AI risks blending a CSM engagement interpretation with an experiment analytics interpretation on the same dataset.

selected.label: "Renewal rate" = Global Renewal Rate / Product Group Renewal Rate metrics (DWH_RENEWAL_OPPORTUNITY basis) — NOT the Renewal Rate Reporting exec deck datasets
selected.description: Renewal rate figures can be sourced from two distinct layers in the app. In this topic, the authoritative renewal rate metrics are Global Renewal Rate and Product Group Renewal Rate (both selected in step 4), built on DWH_RENEWAL_OPPORTUNITY and Product - Opportunities. The Renewal Rate Reporting concept uses a separate cluster — DWH_EXEC_DECK_RENEWAL_RATES_PRODUCT_GROUP, DWH_EXEC_DECK_RENEWAL_RATES_CUSTOMER, etc. — designed for executive deck presentations with potentially different denominators, fiscal-quarter bucketing, and ARR_RENEWAL/ARR_CHURN column definitions. These exec deck datasets were NOT selected in step 3. Do not mix sources in a single renewal rate calculation.
selected.ai_reasoning: The graph shows Renewal Rate Reporting `informs` Customer Renewal (a selected concept) and exposes ARR_RENEWAL/ARR_CHURN columns via its own dataset cluster, creating a risk that the AI pulls from the wrong reporting layer when a user asks an unqualified 'what is our renewal rate?' question.

selected.label: "Renewal pipeline" primary source: DWH_RENEWAL_OPPORTUNITY for canonical ARR/counts; Product - Opportunities for ICP-segmented or stage-movement views — never SFDC_OPPORTUNITY (covers all deal types)
selected.description: Both DWH_RENEWAL_OPPORTUNITY and Product - Opportunities (both selected in step 3) cover renewal opportunities but serve different analytical purposes. DWH_RENEWAL_OPPORTUNITY is the canonical data warehouse table — use it for authoritative renewal ARR totals, close-date cohort reporting, and opportunity-line-level breakdown. Product - Opportunities is the Salesforce-sourced view — use it when filtering by ICP_ACCOUNT status or tracking stage movements as events. The broader SFDC_OPPORTUNITY table (not selected) covers all deal types including new business, expansion, and upsell — it must never be used as the source for CSM renewal pipeline queries as it will inflate figures.
selected.ai_reasoning: SFDC_OPPORTUNITY exists in the app and is superficially related to 'opportunities'; without an explicit disambiguation the AI may use it for renewal queries, pulling in new-business and upsell records that do not belong in CSM renewal reporting.

selected.label: "Partner" = Optimizely channel implementation partner (PARTNER_TYPE in PARTNER_PERFORMANCE_SCORE) — NOT the PARTNER_FLAG that tags partner-type customer accounts in product contract data
selected.description: The word 'partner' appears in two structurally distinct contexts across the app. In this topic, 'partner' exclusively refers to an organisation in Optimizely's channel reseller/implementation network, measured by PARTNER_PERFORMANCE_SCORE and PARTNER_PRODUCT_GROUP_AGGREGATE and segmented by PARTNER_TYPE and PARTNER_REGION. Separately, PARTNER_FLAG is a boolean column in product contract and utilisation datasets (not selected in this topic) that tags customer accounts which are themselves partners — i.e., accounts that also resell Optimizely. These are different entities: a channel partner organisation vs. a customer account flagged as a partner. Do not use PARTNER_FLAG to filter or identify channel partners in this topic.
selected.ai_reasoning: PARTNER_FLAG appears in the Product Contract Utilization concept cluster (graph-connected but not selected), while the three selected partner datasets use PARTNER_TYPE/PARTNER_REGION as the segmentation axis — both use the word 'partner' and the AI must not conflate partner-flagged customer accounts with channel partner performance records.

selected.label: "CTA" always means a Gainsight risk intervention record — never a marketing call-to-action button, campaign link, or click-through prompt
selected.description: In general business, marketing, and product analytics contexts, 'CTA' commonly means a call-to-action element (button, link, campaign prompt). In the Customer Success Management topic, CTA is exclusively a Gainsight Call-to-Action record representing a triggered risk intervention for an at-risk account (defined fully in step 6). Any query mentioning 'CTA', 'open CTAs', or 'CTA ARR' must resolve to GS_CTA_SUMMARY or GS_CTA_CAMPAIGN — never to marketing campaign tables, Uservoice feature requests, or Zendesk ticket click data, even though those event sources are also selected in this topic.
selected.ai_reasoning: Uservoice Metrics and Zendesk Ticket Metrics (both selected as events in step 5) exist in a context where 'CTA' could plausibly be interpreted as a customer-facing prompt or marketing action; this disambiguation extends the step 6 rule to explicitly block the marketing interpretation across all selected datasets.

selected.label: "Churned ARR" for CSM queries = derived from CHURN DATASET (CHURN_DATE + ANNUAL_PRICE_C) — NOT the aggregate ARR_CHURN column in exec deck renewal reporting tables
selected.description: Two separate ARR churn figures exist in the app with the same conceptual meaning but different granularity and sourcing. The account-level churn record lives in the CHURN DATASET (selected in step 3): CHURN_DATE populated = full cancellation; DOWNGRADE_AMOUNT = partial contraction; ANNUAL_PRICE_C = the ARR value lost. The aggregate ARR_CHURN column lives in DWH_EXEC_DECK_RENEWAL_RATES_* tables (NOT selected in step 3), which roll up churn differently for board-level reporting and may apply different fiscal-quarter boundaries or currency normalisation. When a CSM asks 'how much ARR churned this quarter?' or 'which accounts churned?', always resolve to the CHURN DATASET — not the exec deck tables.
selected.ai_reasoning: ARR_CHURN is a `measured-by` column on the Renewal Rate Reporting concept (graph-connected to selected concepts but not itself selected), while the CHURN DATASET is the step 3 selected authoritative source for account-level churn — without this rule the AI may return exec-deck aggregate figures in response to account-level CSM queries.

8.question:
How should the **Customer Success Management** topic grow over time as new datasets, concepts, and metrics are added to Optimizely Analytics?

Choose an expansion policy that controls how far the AI can automatically incorporate new graph-connected entities without requiring explicit human review.

selected.label: Moderate — Depth 2 · Human-confirmed or above  ✦ Recommended
selected.description: The topic automatically incorporates entities up to 2 graph hops from your 8 root concepts, provided they are human-confirmed or AI-confirmed with high confidence. Candidate additions are surfaced to a topic owner for review before going live. Your step 6–7 exclusion rules are applied as filters during traversal, blocking exec deck tables, SFDC_OPPORTUNITY, and the firmographic ICP flag from automatic inclusion. At depth 2, new Gainsight CTA datasets, additional CS org hierarchy levels, or new partner datasets that compose into your selected concepts would be auto-proposed for review.
selected.ai_reasoning: Moderate balances growth — automatically surfacing new Gainsight or partner datasets that compose into Customer Risk Intervention or Partner Ecosystem Performance — with safety, since all step 6–7 hard exclusions still apply and a human reviews every candidate before it goes live. This is the right default for a mature, actively-maintained CS topic where boundaries are well-defined but the underlying data landscape evolves quarter to quarter.
